sica-synthetic-file-editing.reason: Degenerate for program candidates. SICA's problem statement embeds the complete target file (FileEditProblem.statement contains <TARGET_CONTENT>), and the score is the diff similarity of the edited file to that target, so a program that receives the statement writes the target verbatim and scores 1.0 without any model call. In SICA the benchmark measures an LLM agent's editing efficiency through its utility U = 0.5 score + 0.25 (1 - min(1, cost/$10)) + 0.25 (1 - min(1, time/300 s)); at the suite's model prices the cost term is about 1 for every candidate and the time term depends on network latency and hardware, so it gives no stable signal. Hiding the statement from the program (model-only access) would turn it into a different, prompt-only task.

evidence.locator: Eq. 1 (utility weights 0.5/0.25/0.25, $10 and 300 s normalisers); Table 1 (file editing 0.82 -> 0.91)

sica-synthetic-symbol-location.reason: Saturated by a trivial program. A frozen recreation was built (12 of SICA's 14 repositories pinned before 2025-04-20, 342 import-determined instances, SICA's 0.4/0.4/0.2 path/line/column score with the name column fixed), but a 20-line seed that searches for definition lines and asks the model only when several match scores 1.0 on the 60-instance evaluation sample (60 exact, 8 model calls, USD 0.0026) and 0.963 on all 342 instances without any model help, so the task gives no optimisation signal. Without the well-definedness filter SICA's own construction pairs definitions with unrelated same-name uses and labels function and method columns 5 or 3 characters past the name, which makes scores label noise rather than capability (SICA reports 0.35 -> 0.40). The implementation is kept in commit 6e35bbbe of wp/llm-tools for reference.

flowscout-toolbench-finance.reason: Blocked on data. FlowScout's splits, historical records and workflows are unpublished (the paper's code link is the placeholder anonymous.4open.science/r/xxxx/), and the ToolBench answer trajectories that a replay proxy needs are no longer available from ToolBench's documented sources: on 2026-10-10 the README's Google Drive folder and its direct data.zip file id both return HTTP 404 and the Tsinghua Cloud link answers 'Link does not exist'. Only third-party Hugging Face re-uploads remain (for example nullwwg/toolbench-data, whose 1.76 GB data.zip lists 126,489 answer files, and the partial Adorg/ToolBench copy of an older release) with no published checksum to verify them against; the step that would have compared such a mirror with the official repository's data_example files was declined in this session, so per the package rules the input is treated as blocked. Faithful execution would additionally need live RapidAPI endpoints (StableToolBench's cache server falls back to them on a miss, per the triage).
